Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Astra Communications Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those in conference: To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Astra Communications' Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q2. We achieved robust subscriber growth and fiber expansion milestones, which reflect our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our AstraStream service and its rapid adoption driving engagement across our converged telecom and media offerings. Our investments in 5G network upgrades and fiber-to-the-home buildouts are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty with best-in-class churn rates. Furthermore, we have focused on operational efficiencies and cost discipline, which has allowed us to maintain profitability while deleveraging our balance sheet. Finally, our strategic focus remains on accelerating broadband penetration and providing clear guidance to sustain momentum into 2025.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $16.25 billion, representing a 7.8% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $6.85 billion, with a margin of 42.2%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $4.2 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion and fiber deployments.

Good morning again, everyone. Moving now to our cost of revenue analysis for the second quarter, which totaled $8.47 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year from $8.13 billion in Q2 2023, but flat sequentially from $8.46 billion in Q1 2024. As a percentage of revenue, cost of revenue improved to 52.1% from 54.3% a year ago, thanks to the leverage from our revenue growth, driven by postpaid mobile additions and broadband subscriber gains. This marks the third consecutive quarter of cost of revenue margin expansion, underscoring the success of our operational efficiency programs even amid ongoing inflationary pressures in the telecom and media sectors.

Let me break this down by key components, trends, and drivers, focusing on both the absolute dollar impacts and the strategic levers we're employing to keep this positive trajectory going.

Network operations costs came in at $4.92 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. This remains our largest category at 58% of total cost of revenue, covering cell site leases, interconnect and roaming fees, transmission expenses, and variable network opex linked to traffic volumes. The year-over-year increase of $270 million stemmed mainly from a 12% surge in data consumption per subscriber—now averaging 28 GB per month on our 5G Standalone network—propelled by ultra-HD streaming and AI-driven applications such as real-time video conferencing. We've faced particular pressure from international roaming, which rose 18% due to rebounding post-COVID travel demand, with higher costs in APAC markets where we've grown 5G SA coverage through partnerships with SoftBank and Singtel.

Regionally, U.S. network costs increased 6.2% to $3.1 billion, as C-band spectrum utilization ramped up to 85% in our mid-band deployments. Europe experienced a more moderate 3.9% rise to $1.2 billion, helped by lower energy costs following stabilization after the 2023 Ukraine crisis and our shift to energy-efficient Massive MIMO radios. Latin America showed stronger growth at 9.1%, connected to 4G LTE densification in Brazil and Mexico amid intense competition from América Móvil.

To counter this, we've offset about 40% of the inflation through our Network Function Virtualization and Software-Defined Networking initiatives. Our AI-powered traffic orchestration platform, now covering 70% of our U.S. core, dynamically shifts traffic to underutilized spectrum bands, generating $85 million in quarterly savings—that's a 1.7% drop in per-GB costs. Moving forward, we anticipate network costs to rise in the mid-single digits for the second half of the year, tempered by vendor renegotiations with Ericsson and Nokia aiming for 5-7% reductions in RAN pricing.

Content acquisition and licensing costs reached $2.15 billion, up 3.1% year-over-year. Representing 25% of cost of revenue, these rose $65 million annually but dipped 2.4% sequentially due to smarter slate management in our streaming and linear TV bundles. Major drivers include rising rights fees for premium sports and originals, with NBA and NFL renewals contributing $120 million on an annualized basis—consistent with trends at peers like Comcast's Peacock and Disney's ESPN ecosystem. Streaming-specific costs grew 8% from 4K/HDR bitrate requirements, lifting average encoding costs to $2.50 per viewer-hour, though our ad-supported tier recaptured 15% of that via dynamic ad insertion technology.

In North America, which makes up 65% of this category at $1.4 billion, we saw pressure from lingering effects of the Hollywood strikes on production. EMEA held flat at $450 million, supported by local content investments such as our Premier League co-rights deal with Sky. APAC edged up 5% from K-drama licensing with CJ ENM, in line with our 22% subscriber growth in India through Jio-style bundling.

We're addressing this strategically with vertical integration: our in-house studios handled 45% of Q2 originals, cutting acquisition spend by 12% compared to third-party deals. We've also introduced "Flex Content" contracts with Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery, linking fees to actual viewership measured by Nielsen and Comscore, which yielded $40 million in rebates this quarter. We expect content inflation to moderate to 2-4% for full-year 2024 as multi-year deals cap escalators below CPI.

Customer premises equipment and installation costs were $1.08 billion, up 1.9% year-over-year. Including handsets, ONT gateways, and DOCSIS 4.0 modems, this increased $20 million annually but fell 4.1% sequentially with supply chain improvements. Volumes held steady at 2.8 million units shipped, but a mix shift to higher-ARPU fiber ONTs—now 55% of broadband installs—pushed per-unit costs to $285 from $265. Promotional subsidies for our 5G mmWave Unlimited plan added $15 million, in line with competitive offers like T-Mobile's Go5G.

Europe and APAC saw declines of 3% and 2%, respectively, from bulk buys with Qualcomm and Broadcom as chip prices softened after last year's inventory surplus. U.S. costs rose 4% tied to FTTH buildouts now reaching 45% of our 50 million-location footprint, similar to Verizon Fios growth.

Efficiency gains include "zero-touch provisioning" from Open RAN pilots, cutting install labor by 25% and costs per home passed to $450. Deals with Best Buy and Amazon for self-install kits trimmed field operations by $30 million quarter-over-quarter. We foresee CPE costs stabilizing or declining slightly in the second half as 5G device penetration nears 75%.

Other cost of revenue came to $320 million, down 2.1% year-over-year. This includes billing support, bad debt, and agency commissions, with a $7 million drop aided by stabilized postpaid ARPU at $58 and churn below 0.85%—our best in five years. Bad debt fell 15% thanks to improved AI credit scoring, while MVNO wholesale costs stayed level despite capacity deals akin to those with Dish Network.

Overall, cost of revenue grew slower than revenue for the fifth straight quarter, boosting gross margins by 220 basis points year-over-year to 47.9%. Headwinds from higher data traffic volumes up 12% and industry-wide content inflation around 6% per Deloitte were partly offset by $320 million in savings from automation, better procurement, and a shift to higher-margin fiber and wireless services. Our adjusted cost of revenue per household passed improved 3% to $168, showing scale in converged bundles like TeleMedia One, now at 18 million subscribers.

On strategy, we're pushing Open RAN to 30% of new sites by year-end for 10-15% RAN opex savings like Rakuten Mobile, investing $500 million in edge computing with AWS to cut peering fees by 20% through localized CDN traffic, and eyeing M&A in content such as potential Paramount+ tuck-ins for Warner Bros. Discovery-style synergies. For Q3, we guide cost of revenue to $8.5 to $8.6 billion, or about 52% of revenues, with full-year growth at 4-5%—below our 8-10% top-line view. This sets us up for over 150 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion in 2024, ahead of peers as we monetize 5G and stabilize streaming.

Before shifting gears, let me provide our forward-looking guidance on subscriber growth and revenue for Q1 2025 and full fiscal year 2025. As you know, Astra Communications sits at the nexus of telecommunications and media, with key segments in wireless including 5G mobile and IoT, fixed broadband via FTTH, and our direct-to-consumer streaming platform AstraStream, which ended Q2 with over 45 million paid subscribers globally.

On subscribers, we're guiding to mid-single-digit sequential growth in Q1 2025—specifically 3% to 4% quarter-over-quarter—lifting our total consolidated base to 285 million to 290 million. Wireless should see 2.5% to 3.5% QoQ growth to 178 million to 180 million postpaid lines, powered by 5G Ultra Wideband covering 95% of the U.S. population and 85% in major European markets like the UK and Germany. Postpaid net adds hit 1.2 million in Q4 2024, boosted by iPhone 16 refresh cycles and bundles with Apple One. ARPU stays at $55 to $57, backed by premium 5G plans and IoT attach at 15%.

Fixed broadband expects 4% to 5% QoQ to 52 million to 53 million access lines, with FTTH over 70% of the footprint. Our $2.5 billion capex for fiber overbuilds in U.S. Sunbelt and rural Europe—aligned with the EU's Digital Decade—drives 450,000 to 500,000 quarterly net adds. Churn holds at a leading 0.9%, aided by AI network tweaks dropping latency below 10ms on 80% of fiber.

AstraStream video subscribers aim for 5% to 6% QoQ to 47 million to 48 million paid nets, leveraging streaming consolidation post Disney/Hulu and Warner Bros. Discovery cuts. Our slate with exclusives like the next Echoes of Tomorrow season and Premier League rights, plus edge AI recommendations boosting engagement 18% in tests and viewing to over 25 hours monthly per sub, fuels this.

For full-year 2025, we're lifting subscriber guidance to 8% to 10% YoY growth, ending at 310 million to 315 million—better than our prior 7% view, mirroring Verizon's 5G curves and U.S. BEAD's $42 billion rollout.

Revenue for Q1 2025 should hit $28.5 billion to $29.2 billion, up 4% to 7% YoY at midpoint. Wireless: $17.8 billion to $18.2 billion, +5% YoY from 5G SA upgrades and enterprise private 5G like our $500 million Ford connected vehicle deal. Fixed broadband: $6.2 billion to $6.4 billion, +6% YoY with normalized equipment sales, 4% residential pricing, and gigabit+ at 60% mix lifting service ARPU to $82. Media and other including AstraStream and ads: $4.5 billion to $4.6 billion, +8% YoY as ad loads rise 12%, with our CTV platform via The Trade Desk targeting $1.2 billion programmatic like Roku's playbook.

Full FY 2025 revenue guides to $115 billion to $118 billion, up 5% to 8% YoY from 2024's $110 billion. This includes $2 billion extra from 5G FWA to 3 million households in U.S. suburbs and Latin America via Claro JV. EBITDA margins expand 100 bps to 42%, FCF $14 billion to $15 billion for $8 billion dividends and buybacks.

This embeds tailwinds like U.S. C-band and European 3.6GHz auctions, Open RAN opex cuts of 15% long-term with Nokia/Ericsson. North America drives 60% growth on 5G maturity, Europe 25% via Gigabit Society rules, emerging markets 15% on sub-$200 5G handsets at 40% penetration. Assumes stable macro, 16% capex/revenue, low churn despite T-Mobile pricing and Charter fiber. Our net debt/EBITDA at 2.2x and M&A powder position us well.

Speaking of which, let's turn to our debt levels and leverage ratios—a core strength enabling flexibility. Our consolidated net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio ended the quarter at a solid 3.2x, down 60 basis points sequentially and 650 basis points year-over-year from 3.8x. This is at the low end of our 2.5x to 3.5x target, with plenty of covenant cushion—about 1.5 turns above our 4.5x incurrence test—and room for strategic moves.

Total gross debt is $45.2 billion: $8.1 billion short-term and revolver, $32.4 billion term loans and senior secured notes, $4.7 billion unsecured high-yield bonds. Roughly 85% is fixed-rate at a blended 4.2% cost, down 20 bps after refinancing $3 billion of 2028 maturities into 2032/2035 tranches under 4%. Weighted average maturity is 5.8 years, with under 10% due before 2026 for strong liquidity.

Deleveraging comes from strong FCF: Q2 adjusted EBITDA $3.7 billion up 8% YoY on 5% wireless service growth from 5G Ultra Wideband at 65% of 120 million subs, FTTH passing 15 million YTD, and NexStream+ adding 2.1 million nets via NFL Sunday Ticket and originals for 12% content revenue mix. Disciplined allocation: $1.2 billion share repurchases, $800 million non-core sales like Midwest cable and tower leases to American Tower, echoing Comcast spectrum plays. Capex at 28% of revenue or $12.5 billion yearly for C-band and Open RAN with Nokia/Ericsson, with per-POP costs down 15% as 5G SA launches in 12 metros.

U.S. ops (75% EBITDA) at 2.9x leverage benefit from ARPA subsidies and T-Mobile synergies. Europe via Vodafone JV and Germany/Italy assets at 3.7x from 700 MHz auctions like Deutsche Telekom, offset by FTTH JV with Orange for 10 million homes by 2025, FCF breakeven H2 2025. APAC (15% EBITDA) at 2.4x on India Airtel 5G and edge for gaming/AR/VR.

This profile fuels consolidation: regional MSOs for fiber-wireless, content tuck-ins amid Disney+/Netflix churn. Interest coverage 5.8x, $7.2 billion cash plus undrawn revolver for $15 billion liquidity. We guide to 3.0x year-end, 2.8x by FY25 on $10 billion+ FCF after $2 billion dividend increase. Our balance sheet is fortress-like for capex-heavy telecom-media value creation.

Finally, a deeper look at our fiber buildout progress, the foundation of our broadband strategy against cable HFC, T-Mobile 5G Home, and Starlink. Our FTTH network delivers multi-gig symmetric speeds for share gains.

Q2 hit a milestone: homes passed at 5.2 million, up 28% YoY from 4.1 million and 7% sequentially from Q1's 4.9 million. This tracks our $2.8 billion annual capex, 65% to expansion, passing 300,000 incremental homes ahead of 250,000-275,000 guidance via Nokia XGS-PON at 40% of new builds vs. GPON.

Sunbelt leads: Texas/Florida added 150,000 to 1.8/1.2 million totals, with micro-trenching/aerial costs down 12% YoY to $850/passing via Corning partnerships and in-house splicing. Midwest (Ohio/Indiana) 100,000 using $180 million RDOF grants. Atlanta/Phoenix urban 50,000 for 10G PON prep on AI edge workloads.

Adoption is strong: fiber subscribers at 1.35 million, up 32% YoY from 1.02 million, +110,000 sequential—best since Q4 2023 push. Take rate 26%, up 140 bps from Q1's 24.6%, topping industry 20-22% per New Street.

Drivers: Gigabit Everywhere bundle at 55% penetration (up from 48%), with Xumo Stream Box, 5G mobile, ARPU $112 (+$18), 42% video attach (Disney/Paramount+), 65% competitive wins from AT&T/Verizon via door-to-door/digital on 99.99% SLA. Monthly churn 0.9% vs. 1.6% FCC average.

Upgraded 25% PON to XGS-PON for 10Gbps trials in Dallas-Fort Worth at 2.5Gbps sustained for 8K/remote rendering. Open RAN-Ericsson fronthaul pilots for 5G FWA in exurbs hedge BEAD delays.

Fiber now 45% broadband revenue (up from 32%), 52% EBITDA margins vs. 42% copper. Guide FY2024 1.1-1.3 million incremental passings to 6.5 million year-end (60% Texas/Florida), 120,000-140,000 quarterly subs in H2 with $400 million BEAD, Netflix ad-tier ties.

Fiber's monetizing at premium rates where national FTTH is 45% per Fiber Broadband Association, fortifying our media play.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Instructions for those in conference: To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the fiber buildout progress and customer adoption trends?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, John. As Maria outlined in detail, we're thrilled with the acceleration—5.2 million homes passed, up 28% year-over-year, with strong regional execution in Sunbelt markets and robust 26% take rates driving 1.35 million subscribers. Our bundles are resonating, and with XGS-PON scaling, we're positioned for even faster adoption ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for subscriber and revenue growth guidance into next year?

Maria Chen: Yes, Emily. To recap briefly, Q1 2025 subscriber growth mid-single digits to 285-290 million total, with wireless at 178-180 million, broadband 52-53 million, and AstraStream 47-48 million. Revenue $28.5-29.2 billion, building to FY2025 $115-118 billion at 5-8% growth. This leverages 5G FWA ramp, fiber tailwinds, and content momentum, all while managing leverage toward 2.8x.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
